body:
T-01KYSTV5ZB4C4JF92X1CNPS3B2 ("Make .lineage recovery durable across fresh clones and branch switches") shipped a non-lossy branch-identity mechanism: every segment's first entry now carries the EXACT minting `branch` alongside `anchor`, and recoverOpenSegment matches on it instead of the lossy derived filename slug. A round-4 distinct-provider adversarial review (Codex) of that fix found two further gaps, both confirmed by direct code inspection, that were deliberately scoped OUT of that PR (findings 1 and 4 from the same round -- an unsigned segment forging a P5 verdict, and a caller payload overwriting the signed branch claim -- were fixed inline; these two were not, on the judgment that they need real design work rather than a rushed addition to an already-large PR).

Gap 1 -- write-side recovery blindness (HIGH correctness, confidence 0.99): resolveOpenSegment (the WRITE-side resolver) only ever consults peekOpenSegment (the local `.lineage` token), never recoverOpenSegment's exact-branch scan. On a fresh clone with a real committed segment S1 for this branch, if ANY write happens before any read (e.g. `adlc ticket complete` records new evidence as part of the same CI run that will later push/doctor/reassign), resolveOpenSegment mints a brand-new segment S2 (since the token is absent) and writes a token pointing at S2. From that instant, every subsequent read -- even one with allowRecovery:true -- takes peekOpenSegment's fast path (the token now resolves), finds S2, and never scans for S1 again. S1's real evidence becomes permanently invisible for the rest of that checkout's lifetime, exactly the failure mode this whole effort exists to close, just triggered by a different ordering (write-then-read instead of no-token-at-all). Two prior rounds of review scoped resolveOpenSegment as deliberately NOT using recovery ("a writer resolving where to append must stay precise") -- that reasoning is sound for avoiding an ambiguous-append target, but doesn't address the specific case where recovery would find EXACTLY ONE unambiguous match for this branch and the writer mints a needless duplicate anyway.

Gap 2 -- pre-upgrade segments get zero benefit (HIGH compatibility, confidence 1.0): the `branch` field only exists on segments minted by the NEW writer. Every segment already committed before this fix landed (including this repo's own `.adlc/manifest.d/` history, itself the original motivating case for T-MANIFEST-FOREST) has no `branch` field and can never be found by recoverOpenSegment's scan -- only by a still-valid `.lineage` token, which is exactly the thing that doesn't survive a fresh clone. The fix, as shipped, therefore provides zero improvement for any segment history that predates it; the original bug (evidence silently disappearing from push/doctor/reassign/carry-forward on a fresh clone) persists unchanged for all of it.

Both gaps require real design work, not a quick patch:
- Gap 1 touches the segment-writer's atomic .lineage-lock invariants (spec section 7) -- a wrong fix here risks the SAME class of split-segment/race bugs earlier adversarial rounds already found and fixed once. A candidate direction: under the existing lineage lock, when the token is absent/stale, have resolveOpenSegment attempt recoverOpenSegment's exact-branch scan FIRST; continue an unambiguous single match instead of minting; only mint fresh when recovery finds zero candidates; propagate (never silently mint through) a genuine ambiguous-match error, matching the reader-side contract. Needs its own adversarial-review round given how sensitive this code path already is.
- Gap 2 needs either (a) a migration/re-attestation ceremony (mirroring the existing `adlc gate-manifest migrate` cutover ceremony, spec section 8) that appends a NEW, signed, branch-carrying entry anchored into each pre-existing segment without rewriting its already-signed bytes, or (b) an authenticated, tracked lineage index (a small committed mapping file, itself signed) that records branch ownership for segments that predate the `branch` field, resolved as a secondary lookup source. Either needs its own spec-level design pass; this ticket does not prescribe which.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A fresh clone of a branch with a committed segment S1, followed by a NEW evidence-recording write on that same branch BEFORE any consumer reads, still surfaces S1's evidence to push, doctor, reassignment, and carry-forward -- not just the newly-minted S2's. Verify: a new test exercising exactly clone -> write -> read, asserting evidence recorded before the write is still visible after it.
2. Where gap 1's fix cannot safely avoid minting a new segment (e.g. recovery is genuinely ambiguous), the writer's choice is documented and the reader-side ambiguity contract still holds -- no consumer silently loses visibility into real evidence without a fail-closed error.
3. At least one committed-before-this-fix (branch-less) segment fixture, generated using this repo's OWN pre-fix `resolveOpenSegment`/segment-writer code (or a hand-built equivalent with no `branch` field), is recoverable by SOME documented, deliberately scoped mechanism after this ticket -- not merely acknowledged as a permanent gap. Verify: a new test using a segment fixture with no `branch` field, proving it becomes recoverable (or the acceptance criterion is revised here with an explicit, reviewed rationale for why it cannot be, e.g. a security property that makes retroactive branch-claims fundamentally untrustworthy).
4. Full suite green: npm test. Mutation-gate clean: node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12.
5. This ticket's implementing diff undergoes its own distinct-provider adversarial review before merge, per this project's standard process for trust-root-tier packages (the review's findings are triaged on their own merits, not pre-scored by this ticket).

Surfaced by a distinct-provider adversarial review (Codex) of the branch-identity fix (fix/t-lineage-durability, T-MANIFEST-FOREST), round 4; findings 2 and 3 of that round (confidence 0.99 and 1.0 respectively). Deliberately deferred rather than folded into that same PR: both need real, separately-reviewed design work on code paths (the atomic segment-writer lock, and any new re-attestation ceremony) that are trust-root-tier and have already needed multiple correction rounds -- rushing either risks reintroducing exactly the class of bug this whole line of work exists to close.

UPDATE (round 7 of the same review sequence, this same follow-up ticket now tracked from fix/t-lineage-durability): a related, additional gap in the identity scheme itself, not just its scope -- Gap 3, branch-name reuse over time (confidence 0.92). Git branch names are not durable identities: a branch can be deleted and its name later reused by an unrelated fork or contributor for a completely different purpose. A signed segment from a now-deleted `feat/x` remains committed and discoverable (manifest history is append-only; nothing ever removes an old segment file). If a NEW, unrelated `feat/x` is later created and a fresh checkout of it loses its `.lineage` token, recovery's exact `branch`-field match finds the OLD segment -- validly signed, exact string match, but for a semantically different lineage. push would publish its statuses and reassignment could re-attest its evidence under the new branch's current ticket IDs. This is NOT closed by exact-match identity (which only solved the CROSS-BRANCH-AT-A-POINT-IN-TIME collision a lossy derived slug allowed); it needs identity durable ACROSS TIME too -- an immutable signed lineage ID (e.g. a UUID minted once per lineage, or a mapping to the commit/fork that first created it) rather than treating the branch name as anything more than display metadata. This is the SAME underlying theme as gaps 1 and 2 above (a branch name, lossy or exact, is not durable enough for long-lived recovery) and should be designed together with them, not as a separate ticket.

Acceptance criterion 6 (extends the four above): recovery is not fooled by an old, validly-signed segment whose branch name has been reused by an unrelated, later lineage. Verify: a new test that signs a segment for `feat/x`, deletes that branch (or otherwise makes it unreachable), creates a genuinely different `feat/x` later, and confirms recovery does not attribute the old segment's evidence to the new one.

UPDATE (round 9 of the same review sequence, this same follow-up ticket now tracked from fix/t-lineage-durability): a concrete OPERATIONAL consequence of gap 3's root cause, not a separate gap -- detached HEAD (a common CI checkout shape, e.g. a PR SHA checked out directly) has NO branch name to identify with AT ALL, so the fail-closed refusal added for detached-HEAD-with-committed-segments (closing a prior silent-data-loss bug) means push/reassignment simply cannot proceed in that topology once any segment exists, rather than recovering. This is the same underlying problem gap 3 already names -- a durable lineage identity that survives even when no branch name is available at all -- not a new design question requiring its own fix; a piecemeal special-case for detached HEAD without the immutable-identity redesign would risk reintroducing the original silent-omission bug. Acceptance criterion 6 (branch reuse) should be read as covering this case too: whatever durable identity mechanism is designed must resolve correctly with NO branch name available, not just an unreliable one.
title: Close remaining lineage-recovery gaps: write-side blindness and pre-upgrade segments (T-MANIFEST-FOREST)
